title: Introduce econ-smith autotuner for tenant defaults and quant tiers
author: Maya Singh
body:
Summary: This PR adds a lightweight, tenant-aware autotuner (econ-smith) that suggests conservative batching, cache and quantization defaults based on observed token distributions and early-unit-econ probes. The goal is a low-risk first-pass defaults generator that can be applied to new tenants or used to seed the existing defaults-as-code registry.

Motivation: onboarding and tenant churn show that many customers run with overly conservative or overly aggressive defaults leading to cost surprises or increased latency. We need a safe automated suggester that leverages short-running sampling runs and historical telemetry to produce candidate profiles (batching shapes, cache TTLs, quantization tiers) which operations can review or apply automatically under a scoped rollout.

Design: econ-smith is intentionally opinionated and conservative: it runs a short sampling job (configurable sample size) in a dry-run mode against a tenant's recent traffic traces, produces a ranked set of candidate profiles, estimates expected unit econ (tokens/second, cost/token delta), and emits safety signals (latency regression risk, top-k mismatch probability). It consists of three parts: 1) sampler: small, non-invasive replay harness that pulls anonymized, rate-limited traces and runs them through a cost/probe harness; 2) estimator: lightweight statistical models produce expected throughput and cost deltas for candidate quant tiers and batch shapes; 3) prescriptor: a staged suggestion format (dry-run, canary, full rollout) output to the defaults registry with exposure metadata.

Backwards compatibility and safety: suggestions default to "suggested" state and do not take effect until explicitly promoted. When a suggestion is marked "auto-apply" (opt-in at tenant level), the prescriptor uses gradual rollout with canary fraction and health checks described below.

Checklist:
- [x] sampler harness and config file
- [x] estimator model (linear + bootstrapped CI) and unit-econ calculator
- [x] prescriptor that writes suggestions to defaults-as-code registry
- [x] telemetry hooks and metrics (expected_cost_delta, suggested_qtier, suggested_batch_shape, probe_latency_risk)
- [x] unit + e2e smoke tests
- [x] docs: operations guide and review/playbook
- [x] safety gates: max-cost-savings threshold and latency risk cap

Implementation notes:
- Sampling is throttled to <=0.1% of live traffic by default; runs run as a background job in the control plane.
- Estimator currently supports quant tiers: fp16, int8, int4 heuristics and batch shapes up to 16; these are pluggable.
- Prescriptor emits suggestion objects under config/defaults/suggestions/<tenant_id>.yaml and tags them with telemetry slices and a Linear reference when available.
- Safety thresholds are configurable via operator flags; safe defaults are conservative and documented.

Commits (summary):
- feat(econ): add sampler harness and sampling CLI (m: maya/econ-sampler)
- feat(econ): implement estimator with unit-econ model and bootstrapped CI
- feat(econ): prescriptor and suggestion registry writer + staged rollout metadata
- test(econ): add e2e smoke tests and travis-equivalent CI job
- docs(ops): add operations guide with rollout checklist

Changed files (high level):
- redwood/pkg/econ/sampler.go
- redwood/pkg/econ/estimator.go
- redwood/pkg/econ/prescriptor.go
- redwood/cmd/econctl/main.go (new subcommand: econctl sample/propose)
- redwood/config/defaults/suggestions/example_tenant.yaml
- redwood/docs/operations/econ-smith-autotune.md
- redwood/tests/e2e/econ_autotune_test.go
- redwood/telemetry/metrics.yaml (added new metrics)
- redwood/infra/helm/charts/control-plane/values.yaml (operator flags)
- redwood/infra/monitoring/alerts/econ_safety.rules (safety alert rules)
- redwood/Makefile (new targets)
- redwood/pkg/econ/README.md

Testing and CI:
- Unit test coverage: added tests for estimator edge cases and CI for sampler throttling.
- E2E: smoke run that verifies suggestion flow from sample -> estimate -> prescribe.
- CI pipeline: linux/amd64 unit, e2e-smoke (short), lint. The first run had a flaky e2e test (race on temp dir usage) which was fixed in the second commit and the CI status is now green.

Review conversation (summary):
- Ethan Park (reviewer): "Can we make sure the sampler explicitly strips any PII and that sampling is disabled by default in private deployments? Also please add integration tests for the throttling behavior."
- Maya (author): "Sampler strips fields using the existing anonymizer pipeline; added a test for throttling in e2e suite. For private deployments the operator flag `econ.autoSampling=false` is the default. Documented in control-plane Helm values."
- Riley Chen (reviewer): "Estimator looks good, but the unit-econ model needs a clearer explanation of how tokenization variance is handled across models (e.g., GPT-like vs. decoder-only). Add a short note to the estimator README."
- Maya: "Added estimator README section and unit tests that vary tokenization assumptions; estimator exposes 'tokenizer_model_hint' to select the correction factor."

- Anaïs Dupont (reviewer): "Prescriptor write path is fine, but we need a rollback path when rollout health checks fail and also traces for suggested profiles to make audits easier."
- Maya: "Added rollback logic: prescriptor records rollout health snapshots to defaults registry and emits a 'suggestion.rollback' event on failure. Also added audit traces to suggestion YAML (trace_id, sample_window)."

Runtime considerations and limits:
- By default the sampler will not exceed 500 simultaneous probes cluster-wide.
- Suggestions are capped to a maximum of 3 candidate quant tiers to prevent operator overload.
- Default canary fraction is 5% with progressive doubling up to 50% if health checks are satisfied.

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: econ_suggested_cost_delta, econ_probe_success_rate, econ_suggested_qtier, econ_suggestion_latency_risk.
- Dashboards: added a pre-rolled Grafana dashboard (operations guide references it).
- Alerts: econ_suggestion_latency_risk > 0.05 triggers page for SRE; suggestion_apply_failure rate > 0.01 triggers P0.

Security and privacy:
- Sampler uses the same anonymization chain as audit-log-exporter; no raw customer payloads are persisted.
- For Private installs, sampling is off by default and operator must explicitly enable it; suggestions can be kept local and never sent to the hosted defaults registry.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (opt-in): make feature available behind a feature flag and invite 10 pilot tenants.
- Stage 2 (review): collect feedback and adjust estimator tuning.
- Stage 3 (soft defaults): allow operations to apply suggestions as 'tenant defaults' with operator approval.
- Stage 4 (auto-apply beta): opt-in controlled auto-apply with canary and health checks.

Release notes: Adds econ-smith autotuner: a tenant-level suggestion engine that produces conservative batching, caching, and quantization profile suggestions. Suggestions are opt-in by default. See docs/operations/econ-smith-autotune.md for steps and safety controls.
